asks: Asks the commission to drop the interim Banff-Jasper riding and instead keep Jasper in West Yellowhead, create a Rocky Mountain House-Banff riding (Lake Louise and the park, Nordegg, Rocky Mountain House, Caroline, Sundre, parts of Cochrane, Stoney Nakoda, Bighorn, O'Chiese and Sunchild reserves) and a Canmore-Crowsnest Pass riding.

quote: The proposed Rocky Mountain House-Banff electoral district brings together the upper Bow and North Saskatchewan headwaters, adjacent mountain parks, surrounding Crown land, and the communities that depend on these landscapes for their livelihoods. It would include Lake Louise, Saskatchewan River Crossing, Red Deer River Crossing, Nordegg, Cline River, Rocky Mountain House, Caroline, Sundre
note: Writer's own proposed riding joins Rocky Mountain House, Caroline, Nordegg and Sundre in a foothills-mountain district along Highways 11 and 22, with no link to Lacombe. Does not say 'Clearwater County whole' in terms; also adds parts of Cochrane.

quote: It would include Lake Louise, Saskatchewan River Crossing, Red Deer River Crossing, Nordegg, Cline River, Rocky Mountain House, Caroline, Sundre, and portions of Cochrane, along with the principal Stoney Nakoda reserves and the Bighorn, O’Chiese, and Sunchild reserves.
note: Proposes 'Rocky Mountain House-Banff' taking in Banff National Park lands (Lake Louise, Saskatchewan River Crossing) and the Stoney Nakoda reserves; Canmore goes to a separate Canmore-Crowsnest Pass riding. Banff townsite not listed among the places but the text speaks of 'the same electoral district as Banff' and Highway 1 Lake Louise-Banff-Morley traffic, so the townsite may be meant to be inside (that would be B9). Rejects the interim Banff-Jasper riding throughout (memo titled 'Critique of Proposed Banff-Jasper Electoral District Boundaries', p. 48; 'irregular extensions into central Alberta').

quote: Including parts of Cochrane that are functionally tied to these forests within the Rocky Mountain House-Banff electoral district respects this economic relationship.
note: Wants Cochrane divided, with 'portions of Cochrane' (the sawmill/forestry-tied parts) in a Rocky Mountain House-Banff riding; does not say where the rest of Cochrane goes. Not C5 as such because only part of the town and the district is anchored on Rocky Mountain House.

asks: Opposes merging Edmonton-Riverview with Glenora into one large riding; supports the interim report's overall direction.

Supports the joint Okotoks, Diamond Valley and Foothills County submission against a Calgary-Okotoks hybrid, and asks that High River-Vulcan and Banff-Jasper be reconsidered to follow municipal boundaries.
Asks the commission to separate Canmore from Banff and place Canmore with Calgary-adjacent mountain and foothills communities.
Asks that Edmonton-Riverview be kept, that Edmonton and Calgary each get two more seats, and that one northern riding be removed to give Edmonton a seat.
Supports the interim Edmonton-North West boundaries and asks that Edmonton and Calgary be proportionally represented within the 89 seats.
Supports the interim Edmonton-Whitemud boundaries and asks for one more inner-Edmonton riding, such as Edmonton-Riverview.
Asks for more urban representation and suggests exurban and suburban communities (South Calgary/Okotoks given as example) may need their own representation rather than being mixed with rural areas.
Asks that the Edmonton-Rutherford boundary be kept as is and thanks the commission for opposing hybrid ridings.
Asks that no seat be cut from Edmonton and that a riding be added in the centre of Edmonton.
Supports the interim Edmonton-North West boundaries and asks for fewer hybrid ridings, with small and medium-sized cities given their own ridings.
Asks for one more riding in each of Edmonton and Calgary and opposes hybrid urban-rural ridings; accepts the interim Edmonton-Rutherford boundary.

Objects to the interim plan dividing the Rocky Mountain House area into three ridings and cutting the three First Nations west of town off from Rocky Mountain House; asks the commission to reconsider.

quote: The proposed changes will divide our community of Rocky Mountain house in area into three separate electoral divisions. I have particular concerns about the three first Nations communities being excluded from the Rocky Mountain House Lacombe proposed division.
note: Objects to the three-way division and wants the town kept with the First Nations and neighbours to the west on Highway 11. Also says 'We have so much more in common with our neighbours to the immediate West of us on Highway 11 then we do with the the community of Lacombe', which leans toward W1 (current riding 80) but Sundre and the riding itself are not asked for by name; narrower code chosen.

asks: Asks that Jasper stay in West Yellowhead and that existing northern ridings be preserved using the allowed population variances.
Asks the commission to reconsider removing Jasper from West Yellowhead and to protect northern representation.
Supports the interim proposal to place Jasper in a constituency with Banff rather than in West Yellowhead.
Supports keeping Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East as set out in the interim report.

quote: I am writing to express my support for maintaining the current Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East constituencies as outlined in the Interim Report.

asks: Thanks the commission for keeping Spruce Grove out of an Edmonton-based riding and asks that Edmonton's growth be handled inside the city without removing a city seat.
Asks that the interim boundaries for Calgary-Acadia (Kingsland area) be left as recommended.
Asks for more seats for Calgary than the interim report gives and that hybrid ridings mixing urban Calgary with rural areas be avoided.
no request (the record's text holds only the email header and one ticked issue, 'Effective representation'; the message itself is not in the corpus text)
Asks the commission to keep the current boundaries of Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Supports the interim report, including its avoidance of hybrid ridings and added seats for Edmonton and Calgary, and asks that growth in Edmonton's core be recognised.
Asks that the combined Edmonton-Glenora-Riverview be split back into two ridings so Edmonton has 22 districts.
Supports the interim report's Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West, kept as two city ridings and not made into rural-urban hybrids.

quote: I am writing to express my strong support for the recommendations in the October 2025 Interim Report, particularly the decision to maintain Lethbridge's electoral divisions without dividing them into rural-urban (hybrid) constituencies.
note: Rejection is of rural-urban hybrid divisions for Lethbridge in general (no four-way plan was on the table): 'Lethbridge County and the City of Lethbridge have distinct interests that would be diluted if they were merged into shared divisions.'

asks: Asks that the Springbank area west of Calgary be moved from Banff-Kananaskis into Calgary-Bow.
Asks for an additional Edmonton riding and that Edmonton ridings not be shared with surrounding communities.

note: St. Albert named only in a list of places outside Edmonton that 'should also have focused and accurate representation'; no request about St. Albert's own districts.

asks: Proposes detailed map amendments in Edmonton, the Edmonton area (Beaumont whole, Leduc split, Lac Ste. Anne-Brazeau, Barrhead added to an Athabasca-Barrhead-Slave Lake riding) and Calgary, and removal of the four hybrid connections across the Edmonton and Calgary city limits.

quote: Barrhead and Barrhead County are reunited in the Athabasca-Barrhead-Slave Lake riding as there is room for these communities
note: Names a riding containing Slave Lake (the interim Slave Lake-Westlock-Athabasca, with Barrhead added) and so works within the interim arrangement, but never speaks of Lesser Slave Lake or of the Mackenzie riding; no stance coded.

'Cochrane. Springbank' appears only as an OCR'd label on the writer's attached Calgary-area map (unchanged ridings are in grey); the text asks nothing about Cochrane. Map not opened; from map label only.

asks: Opposes the interim Banff-Jasper riding and asks for a Canmore-Crowsnest Pass electoral division.
Supports the interim Calgary-Edgemont boundaries and asks that they be kept in the final report.
Asks for three more electoral divisions in Edmonton and attention to faster growth in Sherwood Park than in Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks the commission to reconsider merging Edmonton-Glenora into Edmonton-Glenora-Riverview.
Is pleased with the interim report, including no hybrid ridings and the two unchanged Red Deer city ridings, and asks that attention be paid to Edmonton's and Calgary's seat counts.

quote: I was pleased as well to see that my particular riding Red Deer South has not changed and that Red Deer North has only changed in so far as the city limits have shifted so they are nice and tight ridings.
note: Also glad hybrid ridings 'are not being added to the mix' (general, not tied to Red Deer by name).

asks: no request in the record text (the message says only 'Thank you for considering my opinion on this matter'; the attached letter about Edmonton-Whitemud is not in the corpus text)
Opposes redrawing the boundaries of Calgary-Shaw.
Village of Delburne council recommends the new Innisfail riding include Delburne, Joffre, Blackfalds and Trochu and be named Delburne-Blackfalds-Innisfail.

note: Red Deer County and the Red Deer Regional Hospital are named, and a Blackfalds-Innisfail rural riding is asked for, but nothing is said about whether any town should share a district with part of the City of Red Deer.

quote: Delburne Council recommends that the new Innisfail electoral boundary includes Delburne, Joffre, Blackfalds, and Trochu, and be named Delburne-
note: Asks that Trochu (Kneehill County) be placed in the Innisfail riding, i.e. outside the Olds/Mountain View-Kneehill riding where the current, interim and both final maps' Olds-area ridings would have it (the minority's O1 lists Trochu inside). Nothing said about Olds, Sundre, Crossfield or Beiseker. A reader could fairly treat this as no OLDS-A stance.

asks: Agrees with the interim report's conclusions and proposed maps (form header: Lethbridge resident, about Lethbridge-West).

quote: Thank you for the interim report. I agree with your conclusions and proposed maps. These are in line with natural dividing lines and keeping our community interests intact.
note: Lethbridge is not named in the message; the form header gives municipality Lethbridge, current division 71 - Lethbridge-East, submission about 70 - Lethbridge-West (pp. 8-9), so the maps agreed with are the interim Lethbridge ridings (rule 2).

asks: Village of Elnora council recommends that Trochu, Huxley, Elnora, Lousana and Delburne be placed in the same provincial constituency.

note: Red Deer County named (and the form header's Sylvan Lake-Innisfail riding); nothing about the City of Red Deer or whether any town should share a district with it.

quote: the Village of Elnora respectfully recommends that Trochu, Huxley, Elnora, Lousana, and Delburne be included within the same provincial constituency
note: Asks that Trochu and Huxley (Kneehill County) share a riding with Elnora, Lousana and Delburne (Red Deer County, in the Innisfail riding). Does not say which riding; either Trochu leaves the Olds/Kneehill riding or the Red Deer County villages join it. Nothing about Olds, Sundre, Crossfield or Beiseker. A reader could fairly treat this as no OLDS-A stance. Compare EBC-2025-2-0654 (Delburne), same Highway 21 request.

asks: Supports the interim expansion of Edmonton-Decore and asks for at least one more Edmonton constituency.
Asks for four MLAs representing Lethbridge in combination with the surrounding rural area.

quote: I see no downside to having 4 MLAs to represent Lethbridge in combination with the surrounding rural area. It is really a mini economic corridor.
note: Header: Lethbridge resident, about 70 - Lethbridge-West. Asks for four city-and-country ridings, against the interim's two city ridings.

asks: Asks for a further seat in Edmonton's core; grateful ridings were kept within municipal boundaries.
Nordegg resident endorses the interim Banff-Jasper constituency and suggests adding the Cardinal River watershed (Mountain Cree Camp) to it.

quote: I’ve lived in Nordegg for the past nine years and I fully endorse the crea2on of the new Banff – Jasper cons2tuency.
note: Quote keeps the text layer's garbled ligatures ('crea2on', 'cons2tuency'). Nordegg is in western Clearwater County, which the interim Banff-Jasper riding takes in; writer says 'Nordegg has much more in common now with Banff and Jasper than it does with the sePled area to the east.' Would also add the Cardinal River watershed.

Neither Rocky Mountain House nor Clearwater County is named. By endorsing Nordegg's place in Banff-Jasper and saying it has less in common with 'the settled area to the east', the writer implicitly accepts the interim division of Clearwater County (W3), but does not say so; no want coded.

quote: Thank you for your interim report with which I totally agree. Both rural and urban constituents have their unique interests and needs which need representation in the Legislature. Diluting them would only exclude one or the others interests from being represented.

Asks for one or two more Calgary electoral divisions than proposed and that the most awkward hybrid ridings on Calgary's edges be revisited.

note: Rejects joining Lethbridge-West to rural areas in any form (covers the four-way plan and lesser joinings); states no positive request, though keeping the city riding as is (L1) is implied. Reacting to the hybrid idea, not to the interim map, which kept two city ridings.
